jobs.description: The asset reconciler (root ADR-0333 §7): every five minutes, for each job it reconciles, compares the version each input of the job's asset is at now (the Iceberg snapshot of a Gold input, or for a pinned input the snapshot its pinning Gold was built from) with the version the asset's last run read (a Gold's recorded source pins; a by-PNU lane's reads.jsonl, which its bake appends), reading only catalog metadata over REST, no Spark and no data file. An asset whose input moved past what it read, that is not running and not waiting on the lane its documents follow, is printed as owed with a key of the versions it owes; its DAG then starts the job once per key (a deterministic run id, so a repeated tick or a lost event never starts it twice), unless a run of it is already queued or running. The trigger only queues the run: it waits for its pool's slots like any other. Writes asset_lag_seconds and asset_unscheduled_seconds per asset for node-exporter (/var/lib/foundation-jobs/metrics/asset-reconcile.prom; the FoundationAsset* alerts), and keeps since when an owed asset has been idle with room in its pool under its state path. Beside them it counts the host's Docker bridge networks against what Docker's address pools hold (docker-networks.prom; FoundationDockerAddressPoolNearlyFull): every job's per-run Compose project takes one, and on 2026-10-29 23 of 31 were taken, 10 by runs whose cleanup had failed. It also names each running container by the cgroup cAdvisor reads it from (docker-containers.prom; FoundationContainerMemoryNearCap, root ADR-0385): cAdvisor runs without the engine's socket. Changes no data: its outcome is always unchanged. It covers the 공매 Gold to bake edge whose event 3912 started nothing on 2026-10-28 (13 hours late), the unit price edges split out by root ADR-0333, and every lane of by_pnu_serving_bake, each its own asset (2026-10-29: its forest-ledger lane failed at 07:41Z and the 10:15 start was deferred by takes_turns, so nothing ran it again). A lane whose last run failed is owed a new start after a backoff (10 minutes doubling to 4 hours); a job serving several lanes is started once for all its owed lanes. The other `inputs` jobs move to it in stage 2.
